clue.text: Silly chick hit on the head

parts.note: a chick is a young bird, and 'bird' is also slang for a girl
to brain someone is to strike them on the head, so hit on the head is brained

explanation.surface: Someone calls a young girl foolish, or a baby bird gets bonked on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with the brain of a bird is foolish, so the compound adjective means stupid.

clue.text: Taxi turned over by vehicle at card game

indicators.note: turned over means the word for taxi is written backwards here

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
a car is a vehicle
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cab flips over beside another car at a card table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taxi turned over' reads like an accident, but 'turned over' just reverses the taxi word; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a casino gambling game played with cards, famously favoured by James Bond.

clue.text: Go up again using scree and in different order

indicators.note: in different order tells us the letters of scree and 'and' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A climber reclimbs a slope of loose stones by a different route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in different order' rearranges SCREE plus AND; 'using' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The prefix re- means again, and to ascend is to climb, so it is a synonym of climbing once more.

indicators.note: a replacement for the words I'm Bob means their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man introduces himself as Bob while standing in for a silly young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacement for' rearranges the letters of I'M BOB; the stray '1' before the quote is a print artefact.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for an attractive young woman thought to lack intelligence.

indicators.note: nearly means the word for everyone loses its final letter

parts.note: all means everyone
ready means prepared

explanation.surface: Almost the whole group is set to go at this point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' drops the last letter of the word for everyone; 'by now' at the end is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means before this moment, the same sense as by now.

parts.note: to nurse is to look after

explanation.surface: Tending a toy train set in the children's room.
explanation.definitionFit: A room in a house set aside for young children to sleep and play in.

indicators.note: in places the organ word within the word for fact

parts.note: a deed is a fact, as in 'in deed', in fact
the liver is a bodily organ

explanation.surface: A donor organ was, in fact, handed to the surgeons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the organ inside the fact word; the link between fact and deed comes from the phrase 'in deed', meaning in fact.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to deliver goods is to hand them over to the recipient.

definitions.meaning: a British slang verb meaning to hoax or trick

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is British slang for a hoax or to fool someone; the other is the North Atlantic food fish.

definitions.meaning: the dairy product made from milk curds

explanation.definitionFit: Idiom 'big cheese' gives a boss or VIP; separately it is the dairy product made from curdled milk.

parts.note: a don is a university teacher
taken as written
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Offering a tutor a short written message.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to make a gift of money or goods to a cause.

indicators.note: off suggests the letters of March are scrambled or gone wrong

explanation.surface: Leaving on a military march with joy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges MARCH; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to enchant or captivate someone, a synonym of pleasing them greatly.

parts.note: rural means of the countryside

indicators.note: conceals means the hide-out word holds the letter a inside it

parts.note: a den is a hide-out
taken as written

explanation.surface: A secret retreat in the countryside is hiding a priest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conceals' puts the article A inside the hide-out word, giving the second word of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Church of England priest who oversees a group of parishes within a diocese.

parts.note: to anchor a ship is to make it fast or secure
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Tying a boat up quickly in time to reach port.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheltered place where ships can drop their anchors, a synonym of a port.

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
to sit is to be seated

explanation.surface: Half a dozen people sit down, then set off to call on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to call on a person or place is to pay it a call.

indicators.note: off suggests the letters of Amy sent are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether Amy was dismissed, then begs forgiveness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges AMY SENT; 'Pardon!' reads as 'sorry?' but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A general official pardon, typically for political offences, so it is a synonym.

clue.text: Country people take time making report

parts.note: a state is a country
men means people

explanation.surface: A nation's citizens take their time compiling an official account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take' and 'making' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a formal account of facts, such as a bank or press release.

definitions.meaning: a tale, especially a long rambling one
spun fibre used for knitting or weaving

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a tall tale someone spins and the spun fibre used for knitting; the two senses meet in 'spinning'.

indicators.note: cooked tells us the letters of beet and till are prepared afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: A beetroot is boiled until done, which lessens it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges BEET TILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to make something seem unimportant or small, to disparage it.

parts.note: a grand is slang for a thousand pounds or dollars
on means working, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: Earning thousands at work, for a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's son is a family member two generations down.

parts.note: BA is British Airways
DE is the postal abbreviation for Delaware

explanation.surface: Someone was asked to fly to Delaware on an airline.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of bid, which can mean to invite, as in bid someone welcome.

clue.text: Former wife gets plenty as model

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse
ample means plentiful, plenty

explanation.surface: A divorced woman gets a big settlement and becomes a fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' and 'as' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a pattern to be copied or a specimen showing how something should be done.

indicators.note: including means the comparative word wraps around the letter for English

parts.note: redder means more red, more rose-coloured

explanation.surface: Male deer turn pinker in an English setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' puts E inside REDDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A species of large British deer whose males are called stags.

parts.note: re means about or concerning
cords are strings

explanation.surface: Folders full of notes on pieces of string.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: stored documents or archives kept as an account.

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a ridge is a raised strip of land, like a hummock

explanation.surface: A dark mound of earth sits atop a railway viaduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link, B placed before RIDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A viaduct is a kind of structure carrying a road or rail line over a valley, an example of a span.

indicators.note: over means the newspaper's name is turned upside down in this down entry

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

explanation.surface: A student paper's former editor finds themself out of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses SUN to NUS; The Sun is a British tabloid daily.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: not put to work or service, idle.

parts.note: ran means organised, as in ran a meeting

indicators.note: back-to-front means the abbreviation for for example is written in reverse

explanation.surface: Someone arranged a compass, turning it the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-to-front' turns round the Latin abbreviation for 'for example'; compass here means range or scope, not the navigation tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: compass means scope or extent, the span something covers.

clue.text: Agreement on charge for musical instrument

parts.note: an accord is an agreement
an ion is an atom carrying an electric charge

explanation.surface: A deal is struck over the fee for a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link placing the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable bellows-driven instrument with keys or buttons, an example of a squeezebox.

clue.text: Persist after new cure beginning to react

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of cure are made over in a fresh arrangement
beginning to selects the opening letter of react

explanation.surface: A patient keeps going after a fresh remedy starts working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the word cure; 'beginning to' takes the first letter of 'react'; 'after' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep happening again and again, a near-synonym of continuing to occur.

clue.text: Salesman came across little Sidney returning paint

indicators.note: returning means the whole run of salesman, came across and Sidney words is read backwards

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
met means came across
Sid is the short form of the name Sidney

explanation.surface: A salesman bumped into young Sidney on the way home with a tin of paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses REP + MET + SID as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: A distemper is a kind of water-based paint used on walls and scenery.

indicators.note: after places the setback letters following the Roman numeral

parts.note: CI is 101 in Roman numerals
set back, the word set written backwards, gives tes

explanation.surface: A hundred and one quotations follow a reversal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setback' is split in two: the word set, turned back. 101 in Roman numerals comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to quote someone is to mention or refer to their words as evidence.

indicators.note: in signals the answer is found inside the word crescendo

explanation.surface: Ending on a musical build-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the close or conclusion of something.

clue.text: He'd treat damaged conifers and oust greener variety

indicators.note: variety asks for another version of the letters oust greener, rearranged

explanation.surface: An arborist is a greener sort, keen to remove sick trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' rearranges OUST GREENER; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An arborist who cares for damaged trees, a descriptive definition.
